Night bus

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Bus service operating at night
For the 2008 film, see Night Bus (film).
TypePublic transport
First service1913

A night bus is a bus service that operates between the evening and the early morning, when most daytime public transport has stopped.[1] Night buses usually follow simpler routes than daytime services and run less often.[2][citation needed]

Contents

  • 1 History
  • 2 Operation

History

[edit]

Early night services were introduced in several European cities in the first decades of the twentieth century. They mostly served workers in printing, baking and the postal service, whose shifts began long before dawn.[3]

After the Second World War, many networks were cut back as car ownership grew. Ridership recovered from the 1990s onward, when cities began to treat the night economy as a distinct part of urban life.

Operation

[edit]

Most operators run night buses on a small number of trunk routes that meet at central hubs. Timed connections let passengers change buses without long waits.

  • Services usually run every 20 to 60 minutes.
  • Fares are often the same as during the day.
